statement: For each integer n>=1, critical independent bond percolation at p=1/2 on R_n={0,...,n}x{0,...,n-1} with all nearest-neighbor edges has left-to-right open crossing probability exactly 1/2.
assumptions: Free boundary sides; crossing may begin/end at any vertex of the corresponding side; independent fair bond states.
source: owner-own-work derivation in ATTEMPT.md; classical planar self-duality (e.g. van den Berg lecture notes, https://www.few.vu.nl/~jvdberg/percln14.pdf)
proof_or_counterexample: Planar alternative pairs the crossing with a complementary closed-dual top-bottom crossing. Quarter-turn maps the dual event to the same primal left-right event; missing side-aligned edges do not affect crossing. Equal laws at p=1/2 force probability 1/2. Exhaustive check: python -X utf8 verify_crossing.py gives 1/2 for n=1,2,3.
remaining_gap: No result for nonsymmetric domains or exploration interfaces; external mathematical review pending.

statement: Hausdorff convergence of embedded lattice vertex sets and unchanged left/right marked sides alone does not preserve critical crossing probabilities.
assumptions: For n>=2 use R_n as above and S_n its induced subgraph after deleting vertex column floor(n/2); compare both after scaling by 1/n.
proof_or_counterexample: The two scaled vertex sets have Hausdorff distance 1/n, but S_n has no left-right graph path, hence crossing probability 0, whereas R_n has probability 1/2 by C0017-SPECIAL-01. Exhaustive check gives 0 at n=2,3.
remaining_gap: This only refutes a stronger auxiliary bridge; it does not refute C0017 or canonical square-domain approximations. External mathematical review pending.

statement: A k-edge separating corridor between two edge-disjoint chamber graphs has connection probability p^k q_L q_R under independent Bernoulli(p) bonds.
assumptions: Finite graph; each corridor edge is a bridge; no other identifications; independent edge sets.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently decomposed source-to-sink event into three events on pairwise disjoint edge sets; product follows from genuine independence. Equality when terminals are the corridor endpoints.
remaining_gap: No implication for general square-domain crossing law.

statement: The specified Jordan corridor domains D_n converge in closure/boundary Hausdorff distance, area and unmarked kernel to the square, while critical induced-graph crossings decay at most 2^(-floor(sqrt(n))-1).
assumptions: n>=81; closure lattice vertices; free p=1/2 bonds; fixed corner marks; formulas in w414 ATTEMPT.md.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently counted one surviving corridor row and k mandatory edges, checked area k(n-1)/n^2 and missing vertices (k-1)n, and verified compact-kernel inclusion. Canonical full square has crossing >=1/2 because it contains R_n of C0017-SPECIAL-01.
remaining_gap: Only refutes an unmarked approximation bridge; properly marked C0017 remains unproved.

statement: For w414's D_n the normalized Riemann-map preimages of the two left corner marks have chord distance at most 8/n.
assumptions: n>=81; Jordan extension; harmonic measure from z0=(1/2,1/2); gate length 1/n and horizontal separation s>=1/4.
proof_or_counterexample: Exit on the left-chamber arc forces a gate hit. The half-plane Poisson density integrates to <=1/(pi*n*s)<=4/(pi*n); conformal harmonic measure converts to arc angle <=8/n and hence chord distance <=8/n.
remaining_gap: Does not identify any C0017 scaling limit; assumes the precise boundary arc and free domain convention.

statement: For the induced graph in the closed 2delta-by-delta rectangle, the critical horizontal crossing is 1/4 while its aspect-2 Cardy comparison is <(8/961)^(1/3)<1/4.
assumptions: Three lattice vertices on center row; free bonds; Cardy horizontal aspect r=2 with x=lambda(2i)=(sqrt(2)-1)^4.
proof_or_counterexample: Two independent bonds give 1/4. Descending quadratic elliptic transform from x=1/2 doubles r to 2 and yields x; x<1/32 and beta integral bounds give C(x)^3<8/961<1/64.
remaining_gap: Counterexample is to uniform-in-domain approximation only; fixed-domain C0017 untouched.

statement: A horizontally stretched critical triangular-site lattice retains RSW and unique fixed-quad crossing limits but fails Euclidean conformal invariance for unit-square horizontal versus vertical crossings.
assumptions: s>1 affine stretch of embedding; Smirnov triangular-site theorem; Cardy F(r) strictly decreases with horizontal width/height r.
proof_or_counterexample: Graph isomorphism preserves product colors and criticality, and inverse-affine pullback transfers RSW/limits. Unit-square horizontal and vertical probabilities become F(1/s)>1/2 and F(s)<1/2, contradicting quarter-turn Euclidean conformal symmetry.
remaining_gap: Effective isotropy is missing; stretched triangular-site model is outside square-bond C0017.
